purpose: Per-level sampling distribution, junction rules and checks for generative use of the PolyPose polyrigid transform on labelled spine CT. The transform is published (Gopalakrishnan, Dey, Golland, NeurIPS 2025); only the sampling distribution, the junction rules and the checks are ours.

conventions.angle_sign: delta > 0 = more lordosis at that segment (extension direction); delta < 0 = less lordosis (flexion direction). Kyphosis-positive quantities (TLK) are reported with the opposite sign by measure_sagittal.py and converted at the boundary.
conventions.segment_naming: a segment is named upper-lower (L4-L5); its delta is the relative rotation of the upper body about the segment hinge with the lower body held.
conventions.hinge: centre of the intervertebral disc below the moving body: midpoint of the upper body's inferior plate centroid and the lower body's superior plate centroid, both from measure_sagittal.py (the release surface fit). Rotation axis = patient left-right axis (bicoxofemoral vector where femoral heads exist, else image x).
conventions.chain: absolute pose of body k = product of the relative hinge rotations of every mobile segment between k and the pelvis; the pelvis (sacrum, hips, femora, and any body fused to the sacrum) is the identity.
conventions.frame: analysis in the RAS canonical frame of nib.as_closest_canonical; volumes are never reoriented when written; axcodes are read and recorded.
conventions.label_ids: resolved with ostk.labels.labels_for(volume); the VerSe-native map (L1=20 ... L6=25, sacrum=26, T13=28, hips 30/31, femora 32/33) is required; id 29 is retired in v11 and never gated on.

polypose.mechanism: src/polypose/weights/weights.py compute_weights(subject, labels: list|list[list], weightfn='gravity'|'invdf'|'exp', normalize=True): per rigid body, a distance transform of the union of its label ids, weight = mass/(D^2+1) (gravity), normalised per voxel. src/polypose/warp/polyrigid.py PolyRigid(drr, weights[K,D,H,W], poses_rot[K,3], poses_xyz[K,3]): log-Euclidean weighted average of the K se(3) poses per voxel, exponentiated. warp.py: volume via grid_sample bilinear/border, mask via nearest; Warp.jacdet gives the Jacobian determinant of the field.

ratio_report.ref: reports/Synthetic real ratio X-ray detectors.md (this repo), section 'A recipe for the C-arm level detector'
ratio_report.values: real frames 10-20 % of the sampled mix (synthetic 4:1 to 9:1), never beyond 10:1; 4x epoch-level repetition of real transitional frames; 25-35 % of rendered CTs carry the variant, by CT choice; 200-500 renders per CT; nobody has measured anatomical-variant augmentation

rom_deg.note: Hard caps on the relative rotation of one segment, per direction, from the neutral supine pose. flex = lordosis-reducing, ext = lordosis-increasing, lb and ar are one-side values. Source per row. Values are in vitro at 7.5-10 N m; in vivo totals (Pearcy 1984) are ~14 deg per lumbar joint, i.e. the in vitro flex+ext sums (10.1-17.8) bracket them.

T10-T11.note: Wilke reports two-direction totals 3.5 / 4.2 / 4.8; halved here

segment_share_of_LL.note: How a requested change in L1-S1 lordosis is distributed over lumbar segments before capping: proportional to the published contribution of each segment to standing lordosis. Fused segments get share 0 and the rest are renormalised.
segment_share_of_LL.crosscheck: L4-S1 = 0.679 of LL here; MEANS (shen2023) apex at L4 in 56.6 %; bernhardt1989: lordosis starts at L1-2 and increases caudally

per_segment_draw.mean: share_i * dLL_target for lumbar segments; 0 for thoracolumbar segments (no TLK target)
per_segment_draw.sd: 0.4 * cap in the direction of the mean (cap_ext if mean >= 0 else cap_flex); 0.4 * min(cap_flex, cap_ext) when mean = 0
per_segment_draw.capping: a draw beyond its bound is clipped and the clipped remainder is redistributed over the other mobile lumbar segments in proportion to their shares, once; any remainder after that is recorded as dLL_shortfall in the manifest row and the tolerance check compares against the clipped request
per_segment_draw.translation: none drawn; every translation follows from the hinge rotations
invariants_by_construction: vertebral count and every label id

target_LL.note: dLL_target = LL_target - LL_measured(source), with LL_measured from measure_sagittal.py on the unwarped volume (supine).

reference_supine_distribution.derivation: yukawa2017 standing 49.7 +/- 11.2 minus the 4.6 deg supine offset of chevillotte2018 (54.8 -> 50.2)

target_LL.posture_note: the C-arm frames are prone: prone on a Jackson/OSI frame equals or exceeds standing lordosis (peterson1995, lee2016 +5.3), the 90-90 / flexed-hip frames lose >35 % (peterson1995). The supine CT sits ~4.6 deg below standing. Targets therefore span the supine reference and its lordotic side, not a single posture.
target_LL.rare_class_rule: for L6 / T13 / sacralised variants the target LL is drawn from the SAME reference distribution as ordinary spines (truncated at +/- 2.5 sd), so that lordosis does not separate the classes in the render bank. Rationale: 2-D angles separate LSTV from ordinary at AUC 0.78-0.83 in real life (albano2020), mostly through the fused junction; leaving that as-is would hand the network an angle shortcut for a decision that is a COUNT. PI, which the warp cannot change, keeps its real class association (yokoyama2016, haffer2021, jacob2023).
target_LL.ordinary_fillin_rule: targets for ordinary spines are drawn from the per-5-degree DEFICIT histogram of the ordinary cohort against the reference (cohort_ctsp_release.json thin_bins_ordinary, to be superseded by cohort_grid.json); a source case is chosen, seeded, uniformly among ordinary cases whose measured LL lies within reach of the target (|LL_target - LL_source| <= 0.8 * sum of caps in that direction: 38.7 flexion, 25.9 extension over five lumbar segments) on the over-represented side of the target bin.

deficit_ordinary_vs_reference_supine_yuk.reading: the supine cohort is wider (sd 13.4) than any published series (9.6-11.3) with its excess above 60 deg; fill-in is on the LOW-lordosis side, 25-50 deg, which is also the flexed-frame intraoperative range

junction_rules.note: Multiplier on both sagittal caps (and on lb/ar) of the named segment. 0 = the upper body joins the pelvis rigid body (one inner list in compute_weights). Castellvi grade from the anomaly tables (castellvi_grades.csv / lstv_flag_labels_v2.csv for CTSpinoPelvic1K; verse_suppl_table1.csv castellvi_grading for VerSe), never inferred from label ids.

castellvi_multiplier_sources.I: enlarged transverse process only, no articulation (castellvi1984, konin2010) -> full ROM
castellvi_multiplier_sources.II: pseudo-articulation: pooled II-IV L5/S1 ROM 3.3 vs 7.3 in controls (kuoppala2025) = 0.45; an upper bound for type II alone
castellvi_multiplier_sources.III_IV: osseous fusion by definition (castellvi1984); III/IV transitional disc protected from degeneration (cheng2022); rule: exactly zero relative motion, fused body in the pelvis rigid body. weng2025's residual FE motion comes from a modelled disc and is not used

L6.definition: six lumbar bodies above the sacrum (lumbarised S1), label 25 present
L6.caps: anchored at the sacrum: L6-S1 <- L5-S1, L5-L6 <- L4-L5, L4-L5 <- L3-L4, L3-L4 <- L2-L3, L2-L3 <- L1-L2, L1-L2 <- L1-L2 (top cap reused)
L6.shares: anchored the same way, top share reused, renormalised: L1-L2 0.023, L2-L3 0.023, L3-L4 0.117, L4-L5 0.181, L5-L6 0.252, L6-S1 0.427 -> divided by 1.023
L6.evidence_gap: no published segmental ROM for six-lumbar spines; anchoring at the sacrum is a decision (lumbosacral mechanics are set by the pelvis), stated as such

sacralised_L5.definition: four mobile lumbar bodies; L5 fused to the sacrum (Castellvi III/IV at L5-S1, or the release's sacralization_count / n_lumbar 4)
sacralised_L5.caps: own caps; L4-L5 keeps L4-L5 (kuoppala2025: no excess at the adjacent level)
sacralised_L5.shares: L5-S1 share removed and the rest renormalised: L1-L2 0.040, L2-L3 0.204, L3-L4 0.316, L4-L5 0.440
sacralised_L5.junction: L5-S1 multiplier 0; L5 in the pelvis rigid body
sacralised_L5.note: a partial (Castellvi II) sacralisation is handled by the multiplier, not by this subtype

T13.caps: T12-T13 <- T11-T12 (oxland1992), T13-L1 <- T12-L1 (oxland1992), T11-T12 <- T10-T11 (wilke2017); lumbar as ordinary
T13.evidence_gap: no published ROM or sagittal series for T13 spines; the extra thoracic-type segment takes the thoracolumbar caps

lumbar_rib_L1.definition: hypoplastic rib on L1 (VerSe stump_rib L1; CTSP has_lumbar_rib)
lumbar_rib_L1.rule: ordinary; no evidence of altered motion

four_lumbar_count_without_fusion.definition: four lumbar bodies with a mobile L4-S1 (rare; count anomaly, not a fusion)
four_lumbar_count_without_fusion.rule: ordinary caps with L4-S1 <- L5-S1; flagged for manual review

both_LSTV_and_TLTV.rule: apply the lumbosacral subtype rule and the T13 rule together

unilateral.rule: IIIa (one side fused) counts as fused (a bony bridge blocks sagittal motion); IIa counts as II

compensation_decision.reason: kuoppala2025: total lumbar ROM in LSTV 33.5 vs 38.3 (n.s.) and compensation spread over the superior segments, not the adjacent level; cheng2022 degeneration above III/IV is a long-term load effect, not a ROM value to sample. What IS retained: the requested dLL is distributed over the remaining mobile segments (their caps unchanged), so a fused spine reaches ordinary lordosis with fewer segments, which is the population finding (LL n.s. in yokoyama2016; higher in jacob2023)

rigid_body: any body with multiplier 0 at its caudal junction
pelvis_rule.invariant: PI unchanged within 0.5 deg (re-measured); SS and PT unchanged within 0.5 deg

variants_per_case.rule: V warped variants per real rare CT, rendered at the same renders-per-CT as the source (200-500, ratio_report), so synthetic-anatomy : real-anatomy frames within the rare class = V : 1 <= 10 : 1 by construction; V chosen so that CTs carrying a variant are 25-35 % of rendered CTs: share = N_rare*(V+1) / (N_bank + N_rare*V)

V_full_bank.note: the cap binds; 25 % is reached only at V = 10 on the full bank

variants_per_case.film_level_caveat: against the 30 real L6 films (BUU) the existing physics_rare bank already holds 845 L6 crops (28:1), so a literal 10:1 per real rare film cannot be honoured without discarding renders; the real-film lever is the 4x epoch oversampling of those 30 films (ratio_report, VERIDAH), applied unchanged

ordinary_fillin_variants.rule: one variant per distinct ordinary source case, targets from the deficit histogram (total deficit 158.4 against the supine-shifted Yukawa reference); synthetic ordinary : real ordinary = 160 : 750 = 0.21

variants_per_case.arm_design: MEASURED ARM: train with and without the PolyPose variants at identical real-frame content and identical epoch counts; report per-class recall, PR-AUC and common-class precision on real held-out C-arm frames (body-box convention), paired bootstrap; the result is reported either way

seeding.draw_order: target LL, then segments cranial to caudal (sagittal, lb, ar), then thoracolumbar segments; the order is part of the spec so a row is reproducible

manifest_row: env_hash (sha256 of the pinned requirements + container image digest)

per_vertebra_dice.rule: Dice(warped label_k, rigidly transformed original label_k) >= 0.98 for every k
per_vertebra_dice.note: nearest-neighbour resampling of a rigid motion is the noise floor

fused_junction.rule: relative motion of a body with multiplier 0 against the sacrum = 0: identical se(3) pose parameters, and re-measured junction angle change <= 0.25 deg

pelvic_incidence.rule: |PI_warped - PI_source| <= 0.5 deg; same for SS and PT

lordosis.rule: |dLL_measured - dLL_clipped_request| <= 2.0 deg (LL_L1S1_deg from measure_sagittal.py); noise floor: the same case measured on two label copies differing only in rib ids gave LL 43.83 vs 44.31 (0.5 deg)

thoracolumbar.rule: |dTL_T11L1_measured - requested| <= 2.0 deg where T11 and L1 are in field

wedge.rule: per-body wedge angle unchanged within 0.5 deg (rigid bodies)

body_mask.rule: SPINEPS body mask (tools/body_masks.py) warped through the same field, nearest neighbour; Dice(warped body mask, body mask re-run on the warped CT) reported, threshold 0.95

render.rule: one AP and one lateral DRR per output; bone term present (make_drr_dataset --paths2-only); the spine must be visible: bone-pixel fraction within the source's range and every vertebra's projected box non-empty

population.rule: over the generated set: KS test of LL, TLK and junction angle against the target distribution, and the SD reported beside the reference SD (spread, not median)

environment.grid_modules: apptainer/1.2.2 and singularity/3.5.2 exist as modules ('module load apptainer/1.2.2'); /usr/bin/singularity does not exist, which is what killed the earlier prep
environment.gpu: cupy-cuda12x needs a GPU node: gvohp / galhp, qos gpu, --gres=gpu:1
environment.python: new pinned env 'polypose' built from the repository's requirements.txt at commit 909a9bb; export with 'conda env export --no-builds' AND 'pip freeze' into the run directory; sha256 of both = env_hash
environment.network: no network access at run time; weights and data staged beforehand

grid.scope: CTSpinoPelvic1K v11 labels (802) + VerSe unified masks (374); TotalSegmentator excluded (per-structure label files, no L6/T13 truth)
